replication.target_description: Replication of sexual-orientation differences in desire for toned/defined muscles. Source reports categorical-BMI primary, numeric-BMI robustness, and White-only models for Phase 1 and combined Phase 2; no supplied replication test locator distinguishes them.

es.location: p. 5, Phase 1 primary hypothesis test; p. 7, Phase 2 primary hypothesis test; p. 8, Phase 2 White-only model; Tables 1–6, pp. 12–17

notes: Identity assessment: supplied text identifies SOURCE https://osf.io/download/3cp2d/, title Replication of a Research Claim from Calzo et al., 2013 from Health Psychology, and Joel M. Le Forestier (University of Toronto). It identifies the Calzo et al. claim and project https://osf.io/tvhma/, matching the supplied replication URL/project and lead author. This is a primary empirical replication report with methods, results, references, Tables 1–6 and a figure caption, rather than a preregistration or secondary account. The supplied text does not establish the reference’s full coauthor list or November 18, 2025 date; no PDF was supplied. Only es_value_r is assigned; all other fields are unassigned placeholders. Target remains ambiguous because description, study_r and locators_r are empty and ser_method does not identify a model or printed metric. Candidates for the gay/bisexual-versus-completely-heterosexual contrast: Phase 1 primary B = 0.14, t = 1.36, p = .173, standardized β = .04 (p. 5/Table 1); Phase 1 numeric-BMI B = 0.10, t = 0.98, p = .327, β = .03 (p. 5/Table 2); Phase 1 White-only B = .12, t = 0.95, p = .341, β = .04 (pp. 5–6/Table 3); combined Phase 2 primary B = 0.10, t = 1.52, p = .128, β = .03 (p. 7/Table 4); combined Phase 2 numeric-BMI B = 0.09, narrative t = 1.31, p = .192, β = .03 (p. 8/Table 5, which prints t = 1.30); combined Phase 2 White-only B = 0.17, t = 2.12, p = .034, β = .06 (p. 8/Table 6). B is explicitly unstandardized; β is identified as standardized on pp. 3 and 9. No metric conversion or target selection made. The original-side p. 4 locator does not identify a replication phase or model.
